name: Starter: Galician
about: Galician in real, everyday sentences, with each one's words in Galician order.

words.estar: be (where or how: estou, estás, está…)
words.ser: be (who or what: son, es, é…)
words.irmán: brother; irmá: sister; irmáns: brothers and sisters
words.moito: much, a lot (of); moito gusto: nice to meet you
words.cine: movie theater (ao cine: to the movies)
words.semana: week (a semana que vén: next week)

moito-gusto.about: Literally much pleasure; the same for anyone saying it.

items.text: Un té e unha auga, por favor.
items.means: A tea and a water, please.
wrong: Unha té e unha auga, por favor.
Un té e un auga, por favor.

items.text: Teño un irmán e unha irmá.
items.means: I have a brother and a sister.
wrong: Teño unha irmán e unha irmá.
Teño un irmán e un irmá.

items.means: Excuse me, where is the bathroom?

wrong: Eu falas un pouco de galego.

items.means: I live in a small house.

items.text: A miña nai vai á cidade.
items.means: My mother goes to the city.
wrong: A miña nai vou á cidade.
A miña nai vai a cidade.

items.means: Tomorrow I'm going to the city.

items.text: O meu pai non fala inglés.
wrong: O meu pai non falo inglés.

items.means: Do you have any brothers or sisters?

items.text: Os meus avós viven nunha aldea.
items.means: My grandparents live in a village.
wrong: Meus os avós viven nunha aldea.

items.text: Este é o meu irmán pequeno.
wrong: Este é meu o irmán pequeno.

items.means: What do you do for a living?
I live in a small apartment.
We live in a yellow house.
There's no milk in the fridge.
The keys are on the table.

items.text: Na miña casa hai dous cuartos de baño.
items.means: There are two bathrooms in my house.
wrong: Na miña casa hai dúas cuartos de baño.

items.text: Quero tomar un café con leite.
items.means: I'd like to have a coffee with milk.
wrong: Quero a tomar un café con leite.

items.means: We're going to eat out today.

items.text: Desculpe, onde está a estación de tren?
items.means: Excuse me, where's the train station?
wrong: Desculpe, onde a estación de tren está?

items.means: I'm going to the movies tonight.
wrong: Esta noite vou a o cine.

items.means: We're going to take a taxi.

wrong: O tren sae a as oito.

items.text: Non sei onde está o hotel.
items.means: I don't know where the hotel is.

items.text: Teño que coller o tren das sete.
items.means: I have to catch the seven o'clock train.
wrong: Teño coller o tren das sete.

items.means: I'm going to call you tomorrow.

items.text: Que fas esta fin de semana?
items.means: What are you doing this weekend?
wrong: Que fago esta fin de semana?

items.means: Have you done your homework yet?

items.text: A semana que vén imos á praia.
items.means: Next week we're going to the beach.
wrong: A semana que vén imos a a praia.

concept.line: The verb's ending says who does it, so Galician usually leaves eu and ti out: falo (I speak), falas (you speak), falamos (we speak).
ser says who or what someone or something is, estar where it is and how it is just now: A miña irmá é médica (the my sister is doctor), Está na casa (is in-the house).

words.means: son = I am; es = you are

concept.line: Every noun is masculine or feminine, and o or a, un or unha and the adjectives with it match it: o coche novo, a casa nova, as casas novas.

words.means: teño = I have; tes = you have

concept.line: meu, miña, teu, túa match the thing owned, and usually come after o or a: a miña irmá (the my sister), o teu móbil (the your phone).

words.means: falas = you speak; falo = I speak; fala = speaks
entendo = I understand; entendes = you understand

concept.line: A yes-or-no question can keep a statement's order (Falas inglés?

words.means: vivo = I live; vives = you live; vive = lives
vou = I go; vas = you go; vai = goes

concept.line: en, de, a, con and por join the word for the after them: na casa (in-the house), do meu pai (of-the my father), ao cine (to-the movies), coa miña nai (with-the my mother).

words.means: traballo = I work; traballar = to work
